claims.claim: Suspects cut through the exhaust systems of seven Second Harvest trucks and stole their catalytic converters at the charity's Etobicoke yard over Thanksgiving weekend
Toronto police responded at approximately 12:16 a.m. Sunday, October 11, 2026, to a theft call in the East Mall and North Queen Street area
Police allege the suspect(s) drove into the parking lot, cut the fence, entered on foot, removed several catalytic converters and fled in the same vehicle they arrived in
The suspect vehicle is described as a black, four-door Infiniti G25 sedan with black rims; images were released
Seven of Second Harvest's eight trucks were left out of service; only two could operate the Sunday of the theft
Repairs are estimated at approximately $80,000 and two to three weeks, with the timeline uncertain while damage is assessed, per CEO Lori Nikkel
claims.attributed_to: Lori Nikkel, Second Harvest CEO, via CBC News

claims.claim: Aurora Foods/Aurora Importing donated $60,000 to help replace the catalytic converters
Second Harvest VP Duncan Salisbury told CityNews total costs including rentals and third-party carriers could be in the neighbourhood of $100,000, with at least two suspects seen on security video
claims.attributed_to: Duncan Salisbury, Second Harvest, via CityNews

claims.claim: Second Harvest delivers rescued food to more than 300 non-profit organizations across Toronto
On New Year's Day, four Second Harvest trucks were damaged by what appeared to be water poured into gas tanks; the fence cut in this incident was installed afterward

Acting Supt. Jeff Bangild is scheduled to give an update at 11:30 a.m. October 15 at 22 Division, with police saying Wednesday officers were searching for one or more suspects allegedly behind the theft
No arrest or charged suspect has been announced; no total loss figure has been confirmed by police or the charity beyond the repair estimate
No arrest has been announced in the Second Harvest catalytic converter theft; police describe suspects as sought, not in custody
